correctness.rationale: Direct multiplication gives the commutator coordinate T^(-a-b)((1−T^b)u+(T^a−1)v), and each further step multiplies by T^(-b)−1. For a nonzero exponent c, T^c−1=NQ_c(N) with Q_c(0)=c, so Q_c(N) is invertible. Conditional on exponents, the first step is zero if both exponents vanish and uniform on NV otherwise. At k≥2 it is zero if b=0 and uniform on N^kV otherwise by the coefficient of u. This includes the trivial action and k≥p. Known order supplies r_0 and the bound N^p=0 supplies r_p; identity masses determine the intervening ranks, whose second differences give all multiplicities. For the partitions (p,p−2) and (p−1,p−1), the ranks coincide up to p−2 and differ at p−1. The nonzero stages of the lower central series are determined by N^jV, so the differing classes prove the witnesses are nonisomorphic. The p=3 case independently gives s_1=17/81 for both and s_2=5/9 versus 1.
residual_risks: Recorded enumeration of five finite groups and 411 bounded Jordan partitions is corroboration; the universal claim rests on the conditional surjectivity and rank proof.

Cocke–Ho on word distributions as finite-group invariants
value.rationale: Word distributions give isomorphism invariants, and here a short prefix of identity masses specifies all ranks that govern a modular action. The uniform conditional law covers every individual value, while the explicit same-order counterexample isolates the last necessary observation; this gives a precise recognition threshold rather than a routine calculation of a single commutativity probability.
residual_risks: The reconstruction assumes a group in the specified split family, known p and order, and exact probabilities. It implies no stability bound for empirical probabilities or classification beyond this family.
